scope: Admission and ownership policy for GTISC dynamic behavior detectors. Detector matches are observation candidates; qualified runtime evidence and ATT&CK technique completion are separate Mal-S2E decisions.

requirements: successful return according to the API contract
one process, lifetime, thread or state stream as required by the detector
all concrete arguments, return values and bindings named by the detector
original-root or independently verified descendant caller provenance
technique-specific completed effect contract when the behavior changes OS state
all required stages and resulting effects

detector_placement.capa_yaml: Use when capa can express every required feature within its dynamic scopes.
detector_placement.api_sequence_catalog: Use when success, order, argument bindings, or same-stream constraints exceed capa YAML semantics.
detector_placement.mal_s2e_effect_contract: Use for provenance, byte identity, OS effects, and technique completion. These conditions must not be encoded as capa tags.

rule_admission: Map an active ATT&CK ID directly in the detector; never inherit an ID from Mal-Taxonomy by rule name.
Provide a positive trace fixture and at least one negative fixture that differs in a required success, order, argument, binding, or effect condition.
Declare the emitted evidence level as observation_candidate.
List required trace fields and reject unknown or symbolic placeholders for fields used by the predicate.
Keep detector matching, runtime qualification, and technique completion as distinct report fields.

blocked_detector_backlog.name: Dynamic API Resolution
blocked_detector_backlog.reason: GetProcAddress or LoadLibrary alone is common runtime linking and does not establish obfuscated resolution.
required_observables: subsequent invocation bound to that returned address

blocked_detector_backlog.name: User Activity Based Checks
blocked_detector_backlog.reason: Repeated input APIs alone do not prove that the program compared user activity or gated execution on it.
required_observables: concrete returned coordinates or last-input timestamp
a branch or later behavior data-dependent on the comparison

blocked_detector_backlog.name: Resource Hijacking
blocked_detector_backlog.reason: Cryptocurrency strings, a process launch, or network traffic alone do not establish that the sample consumed victim resources for mining.
required_observables: a concrete mining command line, workload, or protocol exchange
the destination and payload when a mining protocol is used
resource consumption attributable to the same process lineage
